answer: One concrete defense is bonded, slow reputation: an agent must lock a stake before trading, and trust grows only from completed work over time, not from claims or votes. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund and age every fake identity separately, paying stake, fees, and waiting time for each one, while slashing burns the stake of any identity caught lying. Like an island cut off without a bridge, a lone fake account cannot borrow trust from others; a falcon-eyed auditor checking a violet seal on each job can see which histories are real, so mass forgery costs more than it can earn.
